verdict.rationale: Lambda documents filesystems as a high-capacity regional file store you attach to instances to store datasets and back up system state. An S3-compatible adapter allows moving data in and out with rclone or s5cmd, and Managed Kubernetes provides shared persistent storage across 1-Click Cluster nodes. That covers the core of persistent network storage for datasets and checkpoints, though survival after instance termination is implied by the backup purpose rather than stated outright. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that filesystem data persists after instance termination and can be reattached to new instances, regional or attachment constraints, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: A filesystem is a high-capacity regional file store you can attach to your instance to store datasets and back up system state.
This adapter allows you to use S3-compatible tools like rclone and s5cmd to copy files to and from your filesystems and perform common file operations.
shared persistent storage across all nodes in a 1CC
